  may participate in the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 6833) from any phone,

  speak using the call in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &

  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing
  the Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App
  Store), by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 878 9514 9164, Meeting Password: 066081.

  item on the agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  OCTOBER 12, 2021

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN at 7:03 pm remotely via teleconference, in accordance with
Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361) and the continuing state of emergency, including masking and
social distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

NONE.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN requested that the Council consider adding an urgency item to the
agenda regarding the signing of a group letter urging the California Air Resources Board
(CARB) to conduct Green House Gas (GHG) inventories for all cities and counties across the
state.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO AGENDIZE THIS URGENCY ITEM BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

Item agendized under 12. MAYOR & COUNCIL ITEMS.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-G AS FOLLOWS BY
  THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
OCTOBER 12, 2021
 A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF SEPTEMBER & OCTOBER 2021

  APPROVED WARRANTS 64374 THROUGH 64433 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $213,552.78 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 090821 THROUGH
  090921; 100121; 64303V; 64394V; IN THE AMOUNT OF $98,501.36 FOR A
  GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $312,054.14 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 28, 2021

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

D.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 20, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 27, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF OCTOBER 4, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

G.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION 2487 TO AUTHORIZE THE USE OF
  TELECONFERENCE ACCESSIBILITY PROCEDURES TO CONDUCT PUBLIC
  MEETINGS PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361

  ADOPTED RESOLUTION 2487 TO AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO
  IMPLEMENT AND UTILIZE TELECONFERENCE ACCESSIBILITY
  PROCEDURES TO CONDUCT PUBLIC MEETINGS PURSUANT TO
  ASSEMBLY BILL 361.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Public Comment received via eComment from John Tayeks regarding concerns about
Waste Management rates.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  COMMISSION AND COMMITTEE LOCAL APPOINTMENT  LIST  AND
  APPOINTMENT PROCESS FOR EXPIRING TERMS

  Recommendation: That the City Council review the Commission/Committee
  appointment process for expiring terms, and receive and file this report.

City Clerk Pettit provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA recommended that vacancies be publicized in the newspaper
in addition to the City’s website and social media, in order to reach a broader demographic.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF suggested the initial appointment date of each member be
included in the Local Appointment List going forward, for the Council’s information.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
OCTOBER 12, 2021
 City Clerk Pettit explained that the Council would be receiving the annual attendance report
before interviews in order to evaluate attendance each year among the Commissioners and
Committee Members, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

There being no objection, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN ordered this item to be received and filed.

B.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: GEORGE F CANYON NATURE
  CENTER - FUTURE FACILITY USE DISCUSSION

  Recommendation: That the City Council provide input on possible future facility uses of
  a new Nature Center.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted that the later closing times proposed would require
paying staff to be available to close the facility. She stated that her overall concern for use of
this facility is the limited amount of parking spaces. She also noted that a no smoking condition
be applied to the facility, depending on the outcome of the proposed Smoking Ordinance within
the City.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF stated she supports the proposed 9:00 pm closing time to allow
for after-work meetings and so HOAs may use the facility for evening meetings.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN stated that the community needs this space, and that he
believes there will be enough parking, but that we should wait to see the results of the
environmental impact analysis. He stated he supports all of the recommended uses by the
Park & Activities Commission in the staff report.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN expressed concern regarding the amount of parking spaces proposed
for the facility and his concern about parking at the trailhead. He discussed specific parking
needs in relation to the proposed uses, and suggested the Council consider reducing the size
of the building footprint in order to increase the amount of parking.

Assistant City Manager Davis stated that reconfiguring the parking spaces was not discussed
with the Commission, but that it would be discussed with the environmental consultants and
the Traffic Engineer, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA. She also noted that
agreements with nearby facilities or requiring shuttling from other locations would be other
options available for certain activities requiring more parking.

Assistant City Manager Davis stated that the conceptual design and architect agreement for
the facility was approved by Council in July, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF. City
Manager Grammer added that the Council would have an opportunity to once again review the
size of the building and/or parking requirements for the facility after the results of the analysis
are completed.

Discussion ensued about the approved conceptual design and the potential architectural costs
if changes are made in the future to the design.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ summarized that the conceptual design was approved by
Council, the next step is the environmental impact analysis, and the Council will have a more
comprehensive discussion after the results of the analysis are received.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
Public testimony was received by John Rohrer via eComment.

Consensus of the Council to support the future facility uses recommended by the Park &
Activities Commission, to be assessed in the environmental impact analysis and brought back
to the Commission and Council at a future date.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
OCTOBER 12, 2021
 There being no objection, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

C.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: HIGHRIDGE PARK MURAL
  PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council review and approve the Highridge Park mural
  project with a cost not to exceed $5,830 (project cost plus 10% contingency).

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas explained that the artist brought the project idea to
the Commission, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

City Attorney Davis explained that a copyright/work for hire agreement should be required,
allowing the City to make changes to the murals in the future if needed, in response to
COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ suggested considering omitting the coyote in the garage
mural, noting that it has an aviary theme as presented and in order to be sensitive to residents
who may have lost pets from coyotes.

Discussion ensued about the aviary theme of the garage mural, and whether or not to add a
coyote and red fox as proposed by the Commission.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN suggested that a transparent UV coating be added to the murals before
the vinyl coating is added to extend the life of the murals.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF agreed to omitting the coyote in the garage mural.

Assistant City Manager Davis also noted the suggestion to add the Palos Verdes butterfly to
the garage mural as well.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  APPROVE THE HIGHRIDGE PARK MURAL PROJECT WITH A COST NOT
  TO EXCEED $5,830, WITH DIRECTION TO INCLUDE THE PALOS VERDES
  BUTTERFLY IN THE GARAGE MURAL, BUT OMIT THE COYOTE AND RED
  FOX; ADDITIONAL DIRECTION GIVEN TO INCLUDE A COPYRIGHT/WORK
  FOR HIRE AGREEMENT WITH THE ARTIST IN FORM APPROVED BY THE
  CITY ATTORNEY’S OFFICE.

There being no objection, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

D.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: 2021 HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE
  DEBRIEF

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file the attached report.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ commended staff for the successful event both fiscally and
in the number of participants.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN thanked staff for the successful event, and noted that he received
many positive comments regarding the clear markings on the trail for the runners. He also
noted the City did not have a consultant this year, however did very well with sponsorships.
and suggested continuing without a consultant.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
OCTOBER 12, 2021
 Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

There being no objection, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 735 ADDING CHAPTER
  8.40 (REGULATION OF SMOKING) TO THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL
  CODE

  Recommendation: that the City Council conduct the second reading, and adopt
  Ordinance No. 735. In addition, staff seeks direction on whether the City Council
  supports the use of City funds to assist local businesses in preparing and posting the
  required signage, and if so, to what extent (e.g., full or partial costs of signage).

Management Analyst Jessica Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
Public testimony was received from Alix Politanoff from Behavioral Health Services in favor of
the ordinance, and Eileen Hupp on behalf of the Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber of
Commerce and business owner Richard McLennan, both in opposition of the proposed
ordinance.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN stated that he heard from members of the community stating
that this is not the right time to adopt this ordinance and its requirements on local businesses,
and that this is not a major problem in the community. He also noted that today, the Federal
Drug Administration (FDA) authorized an e-cigarette that helps people quit smoking. He
recommended either delaying the adoption of this ordinance to gather more data, or limit the
scope of the ordinance to only ban smoking on trails, in parks and in City facilities.

City Attorney Davis noted that the current code prohibits smoking in the City’s parks, but does
not extend to trails within the City, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ agreed with the need to prohibit smoking in parks, on trails
and any recreational areas, for fire safety. She also highlighted Kick-Ash’s extensive
educational efforts within the schools.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF thanked Eileen Hupp for speaking on behalf of the local
businesses in the City. She also agreed that the timing may not be ideal to adopt the ordinance
as proposed, and stated she supports limiting the ordinance to trails, parks and recreational
facilities.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA discussed the population Kick-Ash reaches with their
education programs in schools, questioned who would handle enforcement, noted she’s seen
very few people smoking at the Promenade, agreed with prohibiting smoking at recreational
facilities in the City, and ultimately suggested postponing the ordinance to further discuss
enforcement, communicate with the school district, and get more data.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN referenced a study done in the City of Beverly Hills which found no
connection between the City’s smoking ban and business volumes at restaurants.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that Beverly Hills’ ordinance was approved in 2017,
and highlighted the timing of the proposed ordinance happening in the middle of the
pandemic.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
OCTOBER 12, 2021
 City Attorney Davis clarified the scoped of the ordinance and the specific types of businesses
that would be effected.
Discussion ensued regarding scenarios within the City’s shopping centers where smoking
would and wouldn’t be allowed.

City Manager Grammer inquired if Council was interested in including City public rights-of –
way, such as sidewalks in residential areas, within the ban.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  DIRECTION GIVEN TO STAFF TO REVISE THE ORDINANCE, LIMITING THE
  SCOPE OF THE ORDINANCE TO INCLUDE ALL CITY-OWNED PUBLIC
  FACILITIES AND ANY FIRE-HAZARD AREAS INCLUDING TRAILS WITHIN
  THE CITY, TO BE BROUGHT BACK TO THE COUNCIL FOR FIRST READING
  AT A FUTURE MEETING.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

City Manager Grammer reported that COVID cases and hospitalization rates continue on a
downward trend. Beginning on October 7, proof of vaccination is now required for all outdoor
mega-events, bars, breweries, wineries, and nightclubs, but Los Angeles County is not
currently considering implementing any stricter requirements at this time. Since the last City
Council meeting, there have been four new COVID cases reported in RHE. Vaccinations have
reached 100% for seniors 65 years and older having received at least one vaccination, and
88% for those ages 12 years and older.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas reported that a Concert in the Park with the PV
Symphonic Band will be held on October 23 beginning at 2:00 pm and the annual Prepared
Peninsula Expo will be held on Sunday, October 24 at Peninsula High School from 10:00 am
to 1:00 pm. The 42nd annual Tracy Austin Doubles Tennis Tournament will be held November
12-14. Lastly, the Holiday House Decorating Contest and annual Parade of Lights will be held
in December.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported that Friday, October 15 will be the Palos Verdes
Peninsula Chamber of Commerce’s Annual Legislative Forum to be held virtually.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also reported that she attended the South Bay Cities Council of
Governments (SBCCOG) Senior Working Group meeting where Planning Manager Jeannie
Naughton spoke about recent Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) legislation and RHE’s ADU
program.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

**Urgency item agendized at the beginning of the meeting**

A.  DISCUSSION REGARDING THE SIGNING OF A GROUP LETTER URGING THE
  CALIFORNIA AIR RESOURCES BOARD (CARB) TO CONDUCT GREEN HOUSE
  GAS (GHG) INVENTORIES FOR ALL CITIES AND COUNTIES ACROSS THE
  STATE

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN made a motion for the Mayor to sign the proposed
  group letter.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
OCTOBER 12, 2021
 There being no objection, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

NONE.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:53 pm MAYOR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the City Council meeting to the next regular
City Council meeting on Tuesday, October 26, 2021, at 7:00 pm for the purpose of a Regular
meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Steve Zuckerman
City Clerk  Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
OCTOBER 12, 2021
